key_points.point: The document advocates for the rapid integration of AI into the core of organizations to move beyond mere experimentation. It argues that leaders must redesign operating models to leverage AI's speed and scale. This aligns with the accelerationist goal of unconstrained growth and capability expansion. The document acknowledges that this requires a deliberate shift in vision and responsibility.

It requires a deliberate shift in which people set a vision and make responsible choices, and AI provides the insights, speed, and scale to deliver against that ambition.

key_points.point: The report asserts that AI is already delivering measurable productivity gains across enterprises. This supports the accelerationist belief that AI is an immediate, effective driver of economic efficiency. key_points.point: The document promotes a strategy of strategic reinvention where AI is used to reshape organizational structures and workflows. factual_claims.claim: Surveyed companies have broadened worker access to AI by 50% in just one year, growing from fewer than 40% to around 60% of workers equipped with sanctioned AI tools.
Only 25% of respondents said their organization has moved 40% or more of their AI experiments into production to date.
54% of companies expect to move 40% or more of their AI experiments into production in the next three to six months.
34% of companies are using AI to deeply transform their businesses, 30% are redesigning key processes, and 37% are using AI at a surface level.
84% of companies have not redesigned jobs or the nature of work itself around AI capabilities.
77% of companies say the location of AI development is a key factor when choosing new technologies.
Nearly 3 in 4 (74%) companies plan to deploy agentic AI within two years.
58% of companies are currently using physical AI, with adoption projected to hit 80% within two years.
42% of companies believe their strategy is highly prepared for AI adoption, while 30% say the same about risk and governance.
73% of organizations are concerned about data privacy and security related to AI tools.
36% of surveyed companies expect at least 10% of their jobs to be fully automated within a year.
